blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has recognized the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) for its contribution to the implementation of electronic notarization (eNotarization), particularly in facilitating compliance with documentary stamp tax (DST) requirements through the BIR’s electronic Documentary Stamp Tax (eDST) system. The court gave its recognition last Oct. 13 during its ceremonial signing of joint memorandum circulars (JMCs) with the Land Registration Authority (LRA) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Deputy Commissioner Larry M. Barcelo, representing Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza, received a token of appreciation from Supreme Court Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin S. Caguioa.
